newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk Vestel sells new shares to funds for $40 mln.
newsitem.headline: Turk Vestel sells new shares to funds for $40 mln.

text.p: Turkish consumer electronics producer Vestel Elektronik Sanayi ve Ticaret A.S. raised 5.7 trillion lira, or $40 million, from the sale of new shares to foreign funds, offer lead manager Turkiye Sinai Kalkinma Bankasi (TSKB) said on Thursday.
Vestel's 750 million new shares were sold at 7,600 lira per 1,000 lira nominal-valued share on the Istanbul Stock Exchange's wholesale market.

"The shares were sold to a total of 68 international investment funds, one third of which were of U.S. origin and the rest were European," TSKB said in a statement, adding that the deal was "the largest foreign institutional sale in Turkey since 1995."
ING Barings and MFI Securities acted as sale agents in the offer fully underwritten by TSKB.
Vestel shares closed at 9,900 lira at midday on the Exchange's national market, up from 9,850 at Wednesday's close.
The publicly owned share capital of Vestel rose to 33 percent from 18 percent. The company plans to use income from the offer in financing capacity increase and modernisation investments.
Vestel raised its capital to four trillion lira from 559.845 by issuing 890.155 million lira of bonuses, or 1.59 bonus per existing share and 2.55 trillion lira of rights.

It waived 750 billion lira of the preemptive rights to sell them to foreign funds. The remaining 1.8 trillion lira of rights, or 3.215 rights per existing share were exercised at 1,000 lira nominal-value per share.
Vestel which produces television, music sets, monitors and video casette recorders, is largely owned by Turkish textile, electronics and tourism group Zorlu Holding.
